title: The Day of the Patient Crocus
skyStory: The last quarter moon, forty-five percent lit, rests in Capricorn, taking its time. Down below, in a muddy garden bed, a single purple crocus has decided to open. It waited all winter for this exact afternoon. Saturn admires its discipline. Venus admires its colour. The moon admires its sense of timing and makes a note to try that sometime.

reading: There is a crocus somewhere near you, about to open. It waited months, under snow and ice, for exactly the right moment. You are waiting on something too, and today is a good day to realize the waiting has been doing quiet work underground.

Do something to celebrate a small thing that finally arrived after a long wait. A package, a reply, a warm day, a finished project. Make it a feast: your favourite meal, a candle at dinner, music while you cook. The [[Knight of Pentacles]] reversed says do not wait for a big reason. A crocus is reason enough. Joy does not need permission.
joel.mission: Celebrate one small, long-awaited thing tonight with a candle at dinner and a toast said out loud to it.
joel.omen: A crocus or any purple flower in the mud. It means something you waited patiently for is finally here.

reading: The shore smells like spring today: salt, mud, wet wood and something green. The tide is coming back to the beach in long, slow sighs. You were born on the darkest day to promise that the light would return. Look around. It has.

Tonight, have a small feast for no reason. Lay the table like it is a holiday. Light something. Play music. Tell a story at dinner with all ten fingers dancing. The Wood Rat knows celebration is not a reward for finishing; it is fuel for continuing. Joel is doing the same thing tonight at the cabin. Raise a glass toward the woods.
nancy.mission: Set the table tonight like it is a holiday dinner, for no reason at all, and light one candle.
nancy.omen: The first green shoots along the shoreline grass. It means the light you promised has arrived, right on schedule.

together.text: Crocus feast night. Both of you lay a fancy table for no reason and send each other a photo of it. Raise a glass at 7 pm sharp toward each other's direction, toasting to the long wait being over.
